XV, 20)]. » Itemque: « Qui vult venire post me, abneget semetipsum, et tollat crucem suam, et sequatur me [n: (Matth. XVI, 24)]. » -- « Manus illius tornatiles, plenae hyacinthis. » Cur tornatiles, nisi quia regulariter, facile, recto ordine cuncta disponit et operatur? Optimus est faber, doctae sunt manus bene pingere, bene sculpere, optime vasa tornare novit. Cur autem aureae, nisi quia ipsius opera omnibus praestantiora sunt? Sicut [1268B] enim aurum caeteris metallis, ita Dei operatio omnibus praestat. Sed quare plenae hyacinthis esse dicuntur? Hyacinthus namque lapis est aerei coloris, sive etiam flos purpuream speciem habens. Manus igitur Domini plenae sunt hyacinthis; sive quia ipsius operatio nos excitat ad regna coelestia. « Invisibilia enim ipsius, ut ait Apostolus, a creatura mundi per ea quae facta sunt intellecta conspiciuntur [n: (Rom. I, 20)]; » sive etiam propter clavorum sanguinem. Sanguis enim et purpura ejusdem coloris sunt. Sunt etiam manus Domini plenae hyacinthis, quia omnia ejus opera admirabili distinctione fiunt. Unde ipse ait: Quoniam « nec Salomon in omni gloria sua coopertus est, sicut unum ex istis [n: (Matth. VI, 29)], » cum de liliis loqueretur. « Venter illius eburneus. » [1268C] Venter, inquit, illius, humanitas et caro, homo Christus de Virgine eburneus natus est, candidus est, et fortis, castus, eburneus venter Mariae; eburneus et Christi; uterque candidus, uterque fortis et castus.

« Distinctus sapphiris. » Sapphirus namque lapis est, sereni coeli habens colorem. Erat igitur Christi venter distinctus sapphiris; quoniam Verbum caro factum, modo coelestia, ut Deus, modo humana, ut verus homo faciebat. Ergo quia venter dicitur, homo et terra intelligitur; quia vero sapphirus dicitur, quem coelicum colorem habere diximus, ille nimirum, qui de coelo descendit, denotatur.

[1268D] « Crura illius columnae marmoreae. » Per crura namque vias et itinera intelligimus, et est causa pro effectu. Crura, inquit, viae et itinera illius non debilia sunt. Non arundo vento agitata; imo columnae. Sed quae columnae? Marmoreae utique, quae frangi [1269A] quidem, flecti autem non possunt. Christus namque occidi potuit, a proposita vero voluntate detorqueri non fuit facultas. « Quae fundatae sunt super bases aureas: » fidem nempe de his quae nos docuit Deus, et sapientiae firmitatem. Christi namque divinitas humanitatem assumptam et regebat, et sustentabat. Possumus autem, et per itinera, incarnationem, passionem, resurrectionem et ascensionem denotare. Quae ideo super aureas bases fundata dicuntur, quia in providentia et consilio Patris (quod nimirum aureum fundamentum est) ante mundi constitutionem inhaeserant. Unde ipse ait: « Non haberes in me potestatem, nisi desuper tibi datum fuisset [n: (Joan. XIX, 11)]. » Hoc autem tale est ac si diceret: Firmissimum mihi est fundamentum, [1269B] quod nisi se volente me occidi non patietur. « Species ejus ut Libani, electus ut cedri. » Hic enim mons omnes illius terrae montes altitudine transcendit; Christi autem montis majestas omnia complet et continet. Denique Libanus candidatio dicitur, Christus autem prae filiis hominum forma est speciosior. Est igitur species ejus ut Libani, alta, et pulchra, et prae omnibus excellentior. « Electus ut cedri. » Cedrus namque arbor est quae excelsa, odorifera, speciosa, imputribilis naturae esse perhibetur. Haec autem omnia Christo conveniunt. « Guttur illius suavis; » id est, verba quae ab ejus ore prodeunt jucunda et suavia sunt, omnique melle dulciora. Sed quid in singulis moror? « Et totus desiderabilis. » Singularia relinquam: summatim, et breviter [1269C] omnia dicam. Quid dicam? Totus amicus meus est desiderabilis, totus est amabilis. Diligamus igitur eum non verbis, sed opere, et veritate, toto corde, tota mente, tota cordis intentione. « Talis est dilectus meus, » cui fideli annulo desponsata sum, nimioque amore et dilectione conjuncta; « et ipse, » et non alius, non Judaeus, non haereticus, « est amicus meus, filiae Jerusalem. » Vere utique amicus, quoniam propter eam sanguinem fudit, qua major dilectio esse non potest.

Versus: Quis interrogare qualis
Attinet, cum non sit talis,
Cui Pater est aequalis
Et Spiritus principalis,
Deus et homo.
Cujus caput purum aurum,
Lux et splendor animarum;
Comae palmae sunt elatae,
Mire floribus ornatae,
Typice sancti.
Oculi non sunt elati,
Sed columbae similati,
Qui super rivos aquarum
Et fluenta Scripturarum
Semper morantur.
Ejus genae sunt suaves,
*624* Nulli ad videndum graves;
Labia sunt pulchra nimis:
[1270A]Myrrha distillat ab illis.
Quid super addam?
Aureae sunt manus ejus,
Eburneus venter ejus,
Hic distinctus est sapphiris,
Illae plenae sunt hyacinthis:
Omnia novit.
Marmoris sunt ejus crura
In stabilitate sua,
Solida nimis et dura,
Nullo modo ruptura:
Credite mihi.
Sicut cedrus exaltatus,
Ut Libanus candidatus,
Majestate cuncta replet,
[1270B]Omnibus odorem praebet,
Deus deorum.
Dulcia sunt ejus verba,
Vera semper et aperta;
Igne sunt examinata
Et a Patribus probata,
Sicut argentum.
Talis est dilectus meus
Et hic est amicus meus,
Cujus explicare laudes
Quia non valemus omnes,
Hic finis erit.




## CAPUT VI.

« Quo abiit dilectus tuus, o pulcherrima mulierum: quo declinavit dilectus tuus, et quaeremus eum [1270C] tecum? » Imperfecti sunt enim qui hic loquuntur: idcirco ubi Deus sit, quo declinaverit, et quo in loco moreretur, quasi ignorantes inquirunt. « Dilectus meus descendit in hortum suum. » Quid est, inquit, quod quaeritis? Nonne vobis notum est quod in hortum suum dilectus meus descendit? Venit utique in hortum suum, visitavit me sponsam et amicam suam. Denique et dixit: non te deseram, neque derelinquam. Ex quo igitur in mundum venit, ex quo me dilectionis vinculo sibi conjunxit, mecum est et mecum habitat. Ad Patrem ivit, me non reliquit; coelos ascendit, me non deseruit. Non ergo dicas, o homo, quo abiit? non dicas quo declinavit? Vis eum quaerere mecum? Fac ut sentias mecum: operare quod ego, vigila ut ego. Duc oleum tecum, si vis ascendere mecum. Non habeo dicis; nec mecum longius ibis. Vigila igitur accensis lampadibus, quatenus ei venienti laetus occurras. Cur autem Ecclesia hortus vocetur jam superius dictum est: « Ad areolam aromatis. » Ad areolam, inquit, aromatis. Per areolam intelligitur quaelibet anima fidelis, quae disciplina coelesti exculta, et diligenter composita, ac laterum parilitate, id est quatuor virtutibus praecipuis exornata, in sanctis operationibus, multa aromata Deo incendenda excolit.

« Ut pascatur in hortis. » Vis hortus fieri? dicis, Volo: munda igitur cor tuum, aufer spinas et tribulos; fac ut floreat anima tua; fac ut liliis et rosis, castitate et simplicitate, caeterisque virtutibus virescat. [1271A] Tunc pascetur in horto tuo, tunc veniet ille, qui dixit: « Si quis aperuerit, intrabo, et coenabo cum illo, et ipse mecum [n: (Apoc. III, 20)]. » -- « Et lilia colligat. » Semper enim Deus lilia colligit, semper animas sibi conjungit. Scimus enim quia fenum est populus; fenum autem baptizatur, de quo Deus lilia colligit. Vovisti Deo servire, promisisti Deo servire in castitate et humilitate, patientia et sobrietate; haec sunt lilia, quae Deo praesentas; haec sunt lilia, quae Dominus colligit. « Ego dilecto meo, et dilectus meus mihi. » Ego, inquit, dilecto meo servio, et per omnia obedio, suaeque in me habitationis praeparo locum. Et dilectus meus mihi auxiliatur, servitutis merita tribuit, et seipsum in me hospitem infert. « Qui pascitur inter lilia, » id est [1271B] in virtutum odore et animarum pulchritudine delectatur. Vox sponsi: « Pulchra es, amica mea, suavis et decora sicut Jerusalem. » Pulchra quidem, quoniam baptizata es. « Suavis autem et decora sicut Jerusalem. » Jerusalem namque *visio pacis* interpretatur. Merito igitur sicut Jerusalem suavis Ecclesia dicitur, siquidem pacem cognoscit et videt, pacem sequitur, et in pacem credit. Unde scriptum est: « Et factus est in pace locus ejus [n: (Psal. LXXV, 3)]. » Quoniam autem superna Jerusalem filia est, idcirco ejus pulchritudinem et decorem habere perhibetur; de qua Apostolus: « Illa, inquit, quae sursum est, Jerusalem libera est, quae est mater nostra [n: (Galat. IV, 26)]. » -- « Terribilis [1271C] ut castrorum acies ordinata. » Terribilis quidem, quia fide et spe, caeterisque virtutibus armata, malignorum spirituum fugat insidias. Terribilis namque erat Petrus, terribilis erat et Paulus. Petrus namque Ananiam cum uxore mori praecepit. Paulus autem adulterum Satanae tradidit. Terribiles fuerunt et caeteri sancti, qui malignos spiritus ex obsessis corporibus exire cogebant. Sed quare ut castrorum acies ordinata esse dicitur? Castrorum namque acies ita ordinantur, ut unusquisque in suo loco positus, locum sibi creditum defendat. Sic autem et in Ecclesia. Stat episcopus ante portas, ne lupus subintret, ne rapiat oves. *625* Sed quid multa? Unusquisque in suo ordine pugnat. Pugnant doctores, pugnant continentes, pugnant et conjugati. Docti sunt in praelio, [1271D] vitia destruunt, et malignos spiritus supplantant. « Averte oculos tuos a me, quia ipsi me a te avolare fecerunt. » Nam quoniam superius sui ostii pessulum Ecclesia aperiens, et Christum in se recipere voluit, ejusque divinitatis secreta nimium rimari coepit; idcirco hic dicitur: « Averte oculos tuos a me. » Unde et Apostolus « non plus sapere, quam oportet [n: (Rom. XII, 3)], » praecepit. Avertamus [1272A] igitur oculos nostros; et qui de terra est, de terra loquatur: nemo quod incomprehensibile est, comprehendere conetur. « Quia ipsi me avolare fecerunt a te. » Quanto enim altius investigatur, tanto magis mentes hominum divina sapientia fugit. Fugit enim Deus Arium, fugit Sabellium, fugit et multos alios haereticos, quoniam obliquis oculis eum inspiciebant, et carnali intuitu, humanaque ratione de his disputabant, quae nisi divina inspiratione scire non possunt. « Capilli tui sicut greges caprarum, quae ascendunt de monte Galaad. » Capilli, inquit, tui, sententiae, et cogitationes, fidelium multitudines, sicut caprarum greges, semper altiora petunt, coelesti cibo saturari cupiunt. Et « quoniam omne datum optimum, et omne donum perfectum [1272B] desursum est, descendens a patre luminum [n: (Jac. I, 17)]; » terrenum victum fastidientes, de coelo sibi venientem cibum exspectant; denique et seipsos Domino sacrificant. « Quae apparuerunt de monte Galaad. » Galaad namque *acervus testimonii* interpretatur. Cur igitur haec duo Testamenta Galaad dicantur, evidenter apparet. » Dentes tui sunt greges « tonsarum ovium, quae ascenderunt de lavacro. Omnes gemellis fetibus, et sterilis non est in eis. Sicut cortex mali punici, sic genae tuae absque oculis tuis. » Laudat Dominus sponsam suam, et eisdem verbis laudat, quibus et superius; nihilque aliud in ea reprehendit, nisi quia eum intuetur, suisque oculis ea cernere persequitur, quae humanus visus videre non potest. Ideoque reclamat.

[1272C] « Averte oculos tuos a me. » Non me quasi localem, quasi mensuralem, quasi alicujus formae statuam intuearis. Aeternus sum, immensus, incomprehensibilis. « Non videbit me homo, et vivet [n: (Exod. XXXIII, 20)]. » -- « Sexaginta sunt reginae. » Quid per reginas, nisi apostolos et doctores, qui alios regunt et docent? Sed quare sexaginta? Sexagenarius enim numerus ex senario et denario conficitur. Sexies namque decem vel decies sex sexaginta faciunt. Et quoniam sex diebus opus suum peregit Deus, non immerito per sex, operum perfectionem intelligimus; per decem autem, legalia decem praecepta signamus. Sic igitur Christi reginae sexaginta sunt; quoniam in Ecclesia rectores, et in [1272D] operibus quidem perfecti, et in legis institutionibus sapientes inveniuntur. « Octoginta concubinae. » Concubinae autem illi intelliguntur, qui sub amicitiae vultu amici domum dissipant, bona distrahunt, legitimaeque uxoris thalamum dolose subintrant, et avidissime violant. Sed quare octoginta? Hic enim numerus ex octo fit, atque decem: octo, enim decem, vel decies octo, octoginta faciunt. Praedicant [1273A] igitur et isti, legalia decem praecepta, sed non ex charitate, ut non ea quae praedicant faciant. Hi enim sunt, de quibus dicitur: « Alligant enim onera gravia et importabilia, et imponunt in humeros hominum, digito autem suo nolunt ea movere [n: (Matth. XXIII, 4)]. » Hi sunt qui adulterant verbum Dei. Isti autem in sex diebus non inveniuntur, quoniam otio dediti in bonis operibus non exercentur. At vero nec sabbatismum, nec requiem habebunt, siquidem diem septimum transierunt. Venient autem ad octavum, in quo fiet resurrectio. « Omnes enim, sive boni sive mali, stabimus ante tribunal Christi [n: (Rom. XIV, 10)]. » De hac autem octava dicitur: « Cur timebo in die mala, iniquitas calcanei mei circumdabit me [n: (Psal. XLVIII, 6)]; » id est in [1273B] die qua mali aeterna ingredientur. Sunt igitur octoginta concubinae, quoniam multi legem praedicant, qui octava die in judicio damnabuntur. Damnabuntur igitur multi monachi et episcopi, qui ex labiis oreque bona defluentes, interius vitia reservantes damnabuntur, in judicio ita audientes: « Ite, maledicti, in ignem aeternum [n: (Matth. XXV, 41)]. » Hoc etiam monachis dicitur verbum, qui soli manentes, hoc quod habent, non recte impendentes, absque dubio in aeternum peribunt. « Et adolescentularum non est numerus. » Quid per adolescentulas, nisi quoscunque fideles baptismatis aqua regeneratos? De quibus dicitur: « Renovabitur ut aquilae juventus tua [n: (Psal. CII, 5)]. » Horum autem numerum solus ille cognovit, qui numerat stellas. [1273C] « Una est columba mea. » Multae, inquit, sunt reginae, multae sunt et concubinae. Una tamen est columba mea, id est sancta et universalis Ecclesia, cui unus Deus *626* est, una fides, unum baptisma, una voluntas, id est cor, eademque anima. Haec autem vere columba dicitur, quia simplex est, spiritualis, humilis et mansueta. Perfecta mea, cui senarius numerus certissime convenit; siquidem a meis operibus non cessat. « Una est matris suae, » id est unica et singularis filia supernae Jerusalem. « Electa genitricis suae. » Quoniam sicut illa coelestem diligit patriam, ita et coelestis patria eam diligit. Sumus igitur filii terrae secundum carnem; sumus autem et filii coeli secundum animam. Haec [1273D] enim terrena, illa vero coelestis est. Serviamus igitur non terrenae matri, imo coelesti. « Viderunt eam filiae. » id est praedictae adolescentulae. [1274A] « et beatissimam praedicaverunt eam [n: (Prov. XXXI, 28)]. » Quis enim prophetarum, vel apostolorum, doctorumve Ecclesiae beatitudinem non praedicavit? Quis sanctorum felicitatem non narravit? Subauditur nullus. « Reginae et concubinae laudaverunt eam. » Namque et apostoli, et doctores eam laudaverunt. Denique et haeretici, et pseudoapostoli eam laudibus extollebant. Multae adhuc concubinae, multi falsi praedicatores, multi numinum, et non Dei sacerdotes Ecclesiam laudant. Ipsa enim est, quae ex multis constans fidelium personis catholicam, id est universalem efficit Ecclesiam.

Versus: Pulchra es, mea dulcis amica,
Pulchris vestibus circumamicta.
[1274B]Sunt tibi castra bene armata,
Bene ordinata, ut vinci nequeant.
Oculos tibi geminos dedi,
Quibus me poteris intueri.
Non oculis haereticorum,
Et philosophorum videri potero.
Sexaginta sunt mihi reginae,
Octoginta vero concubinae;
Possunt amari, possunt laudari,
Non numerari adolescentulae.
Una tamen est columba mea,
Unus est meus amor in ea,
Quam et viderunt, et cognoverunt
Et laudaverunt plurimae filiae.



## CAPUT VI. (cont.)


« Quae est ista, quae progreditur tanquam aurora [1274C] consurgens? » Quae, inquit, qualis, quam pulchra est ista quae progreditur, non otio moratur, sed ad me de virtute in virtutem transeundo conscendit, suaque magnitudine mundum replet, et ubique terrarum diffunditur? « Quasi aurora consurgens, » virtutibus fulgens, serenitate nitens, verum et summum diem cunctis gentibus denuntians. « Pulchra ut luna, » quoniam solius fratris, et sponsi lumine illuminatur. « Electa ut sol. » Quod enim eligitur, aliis praefertur. Electa igitur Ecclesia est, quoniam solis fulgorem imitatur. Denique cum Christus sol, luna autem Ecclesia dicatur, non immerito dicitur electa ut sol. Sicut enim Ecclesia solem, ita et sol justitiae Christus Dominus noster Ecclesiam [1274D] elegit. Unde est illud: « Et cum electo electus eris [n: (Psal. XVII, 17)]. » -- « Terribilis. » Quare terribilis? Quia prudens, quia fortis, quia sapiens, quia « ut [1275A] castrorum acies ordinata » est. Semper vigilans, semper armata, nunquam incauta est. Dicit ergo: « Et praecinxisti me virtute ad bellum, et supplantasti insurgentes in me subtus me [n: (Psal. XVII, 40)]. » -- « Descendi in hortum nucum. » Quid per hortum nucum, nisi Ecclesiam? Cur autem Ecclesia hortus vocetur jam superius dictum est: sed quare nucum? Nux enim suavem reddit odorem. Ejus autem fructus duplici tegmine induitur. Quod autem exterius est, amarum est; secundum autem tenax et durum. Quod vero intrinsecus latet, dulce est atque suave. Sic autem Ecclesia exteriorem vestem, carnem videlicet amaram, miseram, lacrymabilem, horridam et hispidam habet. Sub hac autem illa fortis, candida, et unica tegitur vestis quam ipsa suis manibus [1275B] texuit: virtutes enim virtutibus conjungens, operibusque bonis bona opera connectens, admirabilem sibi composuit vestem; qua induta, inimicorum spernit sagittas. Sub hac autem tegitur anima, mira dulcedine et suavitate, fellis omnisque amaritudinis expers. « Ut viderem poma convallium. » In hunc hortum descendit Christus. Sed quare descendit? Ut convallium poma videret, id est humilitatem et patientiam fidelium. De hac autem valle dicitur: « Omnis vallis implebitur [n: (Luc. III, 5)]. » Descendit in hortum, vidit vallem, cognovit et elegit humiles. « Et inspicerem, si floruisset vinea. » Floret enim vinea Dei, quando ad bonum opus se praeparant sancti. « Et germinassent mala punica. » Mala punica [1275C] sunt martyres, mala punica sunt virgines, mala punica sunt omnes, qui peccatis suis erubescunt. Hi *627* autem semper germinant, hi non spinas et tribulos, imo flores et virtutes generant et nutriunt. « Nescivi. » Vox Synagogae: Tu, inquit, in hortum venisti. Ego autem nescivi, tuum adventum ignoravi. Quare hoc? Quoniam « anima mea conturbavit me; » hoc autem « propter quadrigas Aminadab. » Vidi, inquit, Aminadab, vidi et audivi Christum. Aminadab namque *spontaneus populi sui* interpretatur. Est igitur Christus Aminadab, siquidem pro nobis sanguinem proprium fundere non dubitavit. Hujus autem quadrigas vidit Synagoga. Vidit Mariam, quae in utero et in manibus eum bajulavit. Vidit et carnem ipsam in qua Dominus latebat. Vidit et apostolos, [1275D] quos Christus regebat, et ut bonus auriga dirigebat. Hinc est quod dicitur: « Qui ascendes super equos tuos, et quadrigae tuae salvatio [n: (Habac. III, 8)]. » Hoc vidit Synagoga; ideoque conturbata est. Conturbata est propter Mariam, conturbata est et propter [1276A] carnem, quoniam nec hominem esse, nec matrem habere posse Deum dicebat. Audivit et apostolos praedicare: conturbata est, quoniam contra legem loqui videbantur. Praedicabant enim « Christum crucifixum, Judaeis quidem scandalum; gentibus autem stultitiam [n: (I Cor. I, 23)]. » Vox consolatoria Ecclesiae: « Revertere, revertere Sulamitis, revertere, revertere, ut intueamur te. » Vox quadrigarum, id est apostolorum: Tu, inquit, o Synagoga, ut stulta et incauta eum, qui in hortum descendit, non cognovisti, nec propter ejus quadrigarum strepitum tuam duritiam amisisti. Tu vero Sulamitis, tu populus gentium, tu Ecclesia, revertere. Ubi? Ad Dominum, in patriam, in promissam haereditatem. Sulamitis autem *captiva* vel *despecta* [1276B] interpretatur. Ecclesia vero prius despecta, nunc a viro electa est. Quod quidem Rachel significavit. Est autem captiva, quoniam in praelio capta, malignis spiritibus ablata est. Quater autem « revertere » dicitur, quoniam quatuor sunt Evangelia, quae « revertere, revertere » dicere non cessant. Semper enim ut revertamur, poenitentiam agamus, ad Dominum revertamur, nos admonent. « Ut intueamur te, » id est, ut in tenebras non submergaris; sed in coelesti Jerusalem te nobiscum tuamque pulchritudinem in aeternum videamus.



## CAPUT VII.

« Quid videbis in Sulamite, nisi choros castrorum? » Chori namque castrorum, sicut mos est, et laetantur, et cantant, eosque exornant, arma dilucidant, [1276C] propugnacula muniunt, seipsos ad virtutem et audaciam exornant. In Ecclesia vero laus exsultationis et confessionis resonat; caroque equus animae intelligitur, virtutibus ornatur, arma et Scripturarum sententiae declarantur. alterque alterum ad Dei servitium excitat. Vox Christi ad Ecclesiam: « Quam pulchri sunt gressus tui in calceamentis filia principis! » Pulchri sunt gressus, pulcher est incessus, pulchra est et operatio. Unde Apostolus ait: « Sicut in die honeste ambulemus [n: (Rom. XIII, 13)]. » -- « In calceamentis. » Calceata, inquit, es, ad iter agendum parata es. Dixisti superius, « lavi pedes. » nunc autem calceata es, ne inquinentur. Patientia namque pedes nostros calceat, quoniam sanguinem [1276D] innocentum fundere non dubitavit, et non modo patitur. Possumus, et per calceamenta, prophetarum qui mortui sunt exempla intelligere. Sic autem regis filia, haec filia aeterni principis calceata est. « Juncturae femorum tuorum sicut monilia, quae fabricata [1277A] sunt manu artificis. » Quid per femora, nisi filiorum generationem? In femoribus namque fit generatio. Unde super femur servum suum Abraham jurare fecit, quoniam inde Christum exiturum esse sciebat, cujus nomen, qui Deum timent, in vanum jurare non audent. Dicatur ergo: Junctura femorum tuorum sunt tibi, sicut monilia, id est conjunctio, dilectio, et concordia filiorum. Gloria namque matris filii sunt, nullisque monilibus plus decoratur, quam filiis, si eos bene morigeratos habuerit. Tantoque in his major gloria habenda est, quanto superioris artificis manu dignior et pulchrior operatio instituitur. « Umbilicus tuus crater tornatilis. » Quid per umbilicum nisi apostolos? Sed *628* quare umbilicus? Sicut enim umbilicus in [1277B] medio ventris, ita et apostoli in medio Ecclesiae continent locum. Juxta illud: « In medio Ecclesiae aperiet os suum [n: (Eccli. XV, 5)]. » Sunt igitur apostoli umbilicus. Sed quare crater? Quoniam viva aqua, coelesti nectare, et omnium Scripturarum inundatione replentur. Cur autem tornatilis? Quod enim in torno fit, regulam et ordinem non omittit. Sunt igitur apostoli tornatiles; quoniam veritatis regulam semper observant, rotundi sunt, solidi sunt, non scrupulum, non dignae offensionis obstaculum in eis est reperire. « Nunquam indigens poculis, » quoniam semper plenus est, semper inundat, semperque salutis poculum sitientibus propinat. « Venter tuus sicut acervus tritici. » Per ventrem namque subditorum, imperfectorumque multitudinem intelligimus. [1277C] Ventri quidem omnia corporis membra serviunt; cum pedes portant, dentes nutriunt, oculi ducunt. Sic autem et sunt praedicatores, Ecclesiam sustentant, nutriunt, et illuminant. Venter igitur imperfecti dicuntur, quoniam molliores, et imperfectiores sunt. Hi autem acervo tritici comparantur; quia et multi sunt, et ab uno processerunt. Unde ipse Dominus ait: « Nisi granum frumenti cadens in terram mortuum fuerit, ipsum solum manet; si autem mortuum fuerit, multum fructum affert [n: (Joan. XII, 24)]. » Cecidit igitur in terram, venit in Mariam hoc frumenti granum, ex quo illa fidelium exorta est multitudo, quae acervus tritici hoc in loco vocatur. « Vallatus liliis; » circumdatus virtutibus et doctorum orationibus. [1277D] « Duo ubera sunt duo hinnuli gemelli capreae. » Duo namque ubera duo sunt Testamenta. Una vero capra, una est Ecclesia, quae semper altiora petit, et supernum de coelestibus cibum exspectat. Duo autem hinnuli duo sunt populi, Judaicus videlicet et Gentilis. Quot igitur ubera, tot et filii. Vox Christi: [1278A] « Collum tuum sicut turris eburnea. » Collum namque, oculi, et nasus dicuntur apostoli. Collum quidem, quoniam scutum portant; et Ecclesiam nutriunt, et doctrinae verba depromunt. Oculi autem, quoniam caecos illuminant. Nasus vero, quoniam et sacrae legis virtutumque odorem, et pravae doctrinae haereticorum, vitiorumque fetorem cognoscunt. Collum igitur Ecclesiae, id est quilibet praedicator, turris esse debet, refugium caeterorum, et alta defensio. Unde est illud: « Turris fortitudinis a facie inimici [n: (Psal. LX, 4)]. » Sit autem et eburnea, id est casta, candida et fortis. « Oculi tui sicut piscinae in Hesebon. » Hesebon quidem *cingulum moeroris,* vel *civitas multitudinis* interpretatur. Ecclesia vero multos in se continet, multosque cingit et ligat; multos effeminatos [1278B] succinctis vestibus ad virilia praeparat, multos effrenatos et dissolutos, ne per inania vagentur, in camo et freno constringit. Piscinas autem, quae in Ecclesia sunt, fontem baptismatis intelligimus. In his autem piscatores multos pisces et levant et capiunt. Sunt igitur oculi Ecclesiae, id est sancti praedicatores, et clari, et lucidi sicut piscinae in Hesebon; praesertim cum eorum praedicationes animarum purgatio sint. Quae enim semel in baptismate purgantur, multoties a doctoribus purgari oportet. « Quae sunt in portis filiae multitudinis. » Filia namque multitudinis Ecclesia dicitur, quoniam filiorum multitudinem quotidie parere non cessat. In hujus autem portis sunt istae piscinae; quoniam in ea nemo ingreditur, nisi prius baptizetur. Vis [1278C] ingredi civitatem? descende in piscinam. Vis jungi Ecclesiae? baptizare, et crede.

« Nasus tuus sicut turris Libani. » Libanus enim, qui *candidatio* interpretatur, qui omnibus illius provinciae montibus praeeminet, Christum significat. In hoc autem monte, in hujus lapidis firmitate turris illa sita est, illa apostolorum congregatio fundata est, quae totam Ecclesiam desuper intuetur, et protegit. Unde et episcopi vocantur, quasi supra videntes. Alta est ergo turris, altum est et fundamentum. Non fetorem timet, non aeris perturbationem pertimescit. Coelestia petit, non in vitiorum volutabris jacet. « Quae respicit contra Damascum, » id est contra diabolum et angelos ejus. Damascus enim [1278D] *sanguinis potus* interpretatur. Turris igitur Dei respiciat contra Damascum, id est contra eos, qui sanctorum sanguinem sitiunt. Ea enim ex parte, qua magis timetur, plures ponendi sunt speculatores. « Caput tuum sicut Carmelus. Quid per caput, nisi cor et intellectus? Ut enim caput in [1279A] corpore, sic et intellectus in anima principatum tenet. Carmelus autem *cogitatio circumcisionis* interpretatur. Est igitur Ecclesiae caput sicut Carmelus; magnus est, altus est, non humilia, non carnalia, imo coelestia et spiritualia novit. Non litteram quae occidit, sed spiritum qui vivificat, sequitur; non carnis, sed cordis circumcisionem didicit. « Et comae capitis tui, sicut purpura regis juncta canalibus. » Si enim caput intellectus est, quid *629* erunt comae capitis, nisi cogitationes intellectui adhaerentes. Hae autem purpurae assimilantur, quoniam et de peccatis semper erubescunt, et sanguinis pro Christo diligunt effusionem. Non reges magis in purpura gloriantur, quam sancti in indumento talium cogitationum. Haec est vestis et purpura sanctorum; his teguntur, his [1279B] ornantur; hae sunt junctae canalibus, hae semper lavacrum et purgationem exspectant. Sit igitur sanctis altus intellectus, induantur et ornentur bonis cogitationibus; semper animarum desiderent purgationem

« Quam pulchra es, et quam decora, charissima, in deliciis! » Quibus deliciis? Spiritualis gratiae, id est divinae sapientiae coelestium gaudiorum. « Statura tua, » id est perfecta et alta stabilitas, « assimilata est palmae, » quia firma et recta stat, et nunquam a ventis detorquetur, ejus rami proceri, hujus fructus suavis, hujus viriditas aeterna. Palma victoribus convenit, victoria ab Ecclesia non recedit. « Et ubera tua botri, » id est doctores vel gemina Testamenta, quae aliquando lac, aliquando merum vinum [1279C] nobis propinant. Hoc autem vino qui inebriantur, terrenorum obliviscuntur.

Versus: Ad Deum tuum revertere, Sulamitis,
Apostolorum fidelibus crede dictis:
Eia revertere.
Sunt pedes tui pulchri in calceamentis
Et verba tua prophetarum in exemplis,
Filia principis.
Quid de junctura dicam femorum tuorum?
Qua decoraris ob merita filiorum,
Sicut monilibus.
Per umbilicum omnes illi describuntur,
Ecclesiarum qui in medio loquuntur
[1279D]Spiritualia.
Tritici acervus tuus dicitur venter,
Ab uno grano, quod multiplicatur semper,
Vallatus liliis.
Collum, et nasus, et oculi sunt doctores
Qui ventrem pascunt, pellunt noctem et fetores,
Gravis scientiae.



## CAPUT VII. (cont.)


Christus vel Ecclesia: « Dixi: Ascendam in palmam. » Hoc enim dixit Christus; hoc ante praescivit, [1280A] quod in palmam et virginem, in crucem ascensurus erat. Palma est Maria, quia semper viridis et virgo. Palma est crux, quia victoriae instrumentum. Semper crescit, semper viret, hujus laus aeterna, hujus virtus nunquam senescit. « Et apprehendam fructus ejus. » Fructus dedit venter Mariae, mundi scilicet instaurationem. Fructus dedit, et Christi crux, quoniam ejus sanguine purpurata, mortuos vivere fecit. Vos hujus fructus estis, apostoli, martyres et confessores. O palma! O victrix et admirabilis arbor, quae tantis fructibus decoraris! Ascendit Christus in palmam, apprehendit fructus, quoniam omnia ad se traxit. « Et erunt ubera tua sicut botri vineae. » Ubera namque Ecclesiae et vinum continent, et lac: lacte nutriunt simplices, vino inebriant sapientes. [1280B] Hoc lacte suos filios Ecclesia nutrit, hoc vino et mentes et corda laetificat. Hoc vinum dat sapientiam, hi fecundi calices infantium linguas fecere disertas. « Et odores tui sicut malorum, » id est grati et suaves. Gratus est odor, jucunda sunt poma. Dulces et graves sunt sententiae. Vox Ecclesiae: « Guttur tuum sicut vinum optimum, verba tua dulcia sunt et suavia. » Vinum sunt, sed optimum, quoniam et si profunda sint, dulcedinem tamen et laetitiam denuntiant, non mortem, sed vitam praedicant. Tu enim non vis mortem peccatoris, sed vitam. Vinum namque Moyses dabat, cum, « oculum pro oculo, dentem pro dente [n: (Deut. XIX, 21)], » dicebat. Hoc autem vinum grave videtur, et ad bibendum asperum. « Dignum dilecto meo ad potandum. » Dignum, inquit, [1280C] est, vitale vinum, tam dulce, tam suave; dilectus meus bibat; dignum est ut tam melliflua verba ab ipsius ore distillent. De hoc enim gutture, de hoc vase pretioso vinum illud exivit, quo Ecclesia inebriatur. Gustavit vinum, laudat et pincernam et vinum. Et quasi interrogata an bonum esset vinum, regis esse dignum respondit. « Labiisque et dentibus ejus ad ruminandum. » Quid per labia et dentes, nisi apostolos et doctores? Hi sunt qui praedictum vinum et bibunt, et ruminant. Hi sunt qui divina secreta subtiliter perquirunt. Vinum namque ruminare est Dei testimonia semper et in labiis et in corde volvere. Unde Apostolus ait: « Sine intermissione orate [n: (I Thess. V, 17)]. » Sponsa de [1280D] sponso: « Ego dilecto meo, et ad me conversio ejus. » Ego, inquit, dilecto meo loquor, measque ei voluntates confiteor; ipse autem ad me convertitur, mihi respondet, et me exaudit. « Veni, dilecte mi. » *630* Haec autem vox prophetarum est, omniumque illorum qui Christi adventum exspectabant. « Veni, dilecte mi, » inspice terras, sume carnem. « Egrediamur in agrum, » ut inde spinas et tribulos eradicemus. Colamus agrum, praedicemus gentes, exeat [1281A] jar qui seminat seminare semen suum. « Commoremur in villis; » id est habitemus in gentibus. Rustici enim eramus et indocti. Non legem, non judices, non de judiciis noveramus. Veniens autem Dei Flius in mundum reliquit civitates, reliquit Jerusalem. Unde ipse ait: « Ecce elongavi fugiens, et mansi in solitudine [n: (Psal. LIV, 8)]. » Jam legem habemus, jam urbane loquimur, quoniam rex universalis cum lege et judicibus in villis moratur. » « Mane surgamus ad vineas. » -- « Nox praecessit, dies autem appropinquavit [n: (Rom. XIII, 12)]. » Surgant doctores, quia dies est, ne dormiant, quia nox praecessit. Surge tu, Paule, qui caeteros vigilare admones, amputa Dei vineam, praepara, et munda tuam plantationem. Tu enim plantasti, Apollo rigavit. [1281B] « Videamus si floruit vinea, » id est si jam fidem et doctorum suscepit documenta. Hoc enim ille videbat, hos flores ille desiderabat, cui erat sollicitudo omnium Ecclesiarum. « Si flores fructus parturiunt. » Flores namque fructus parturiunt, cum bona perveniunt ad effectum. Sive cum ea bona, quae incoepimus, ad finem usque perducimus. « Si floruerunt mala punica, » id est si adhuc martyres pro Christo mori non dubitant. Florent denique mala punica, quando humiles et pauperes virtutibus et sanctitate refulgent. Est enim arbor mali punici brevis atque deformis. « Ibique dabo tibi ubera mea. » Ubi? In vineis, tibi mea ubera dabo, tibi meam castitatem servabo, ad tuam laudem et honorem filios lactabo. Fugiant Judaei, fugiant et haeretici, [1281C] quibus nec tangere haec ubera licet. « Mandragorae dederunt odorem in portis nostris; » id est apostoli et doctores, quia aliis quidem erant odor mortis in mortem, aliis odor vitae in vitam [n: (II Cor. II, 16)]. Hi autem in portis nostris, id est in auditu fidelium sui odorem et notitiam dederunt. Sed quare mandragorae isti dicuntur? Mandragora namque sterilitati repugnat. De apostolis autem, et doctoribus superius dictum est, quoniam sterilis non est inter eos. Praeterea his, qui dormire non possunt, mandragora somnum praestat. Hi autem et aeternae vitae quietem cunctis praestant, et eos, qui saeculi sollicitudine vexabantur, omnium terrenorum saepissime oblivisci faciunt. Dant somnum et quietem, dant [1281D] pristinae vitae oblivionem. « Omnia poma nova et vetera, dilecte mi, servavi tibi. » Vetera quidem, quia patriarchas et prophetas; nova vero, quia apostolos et confessores. Hoc autem et de novis veteribusque [1282A] sententiis intelligitur. Custodit utique Ecclesia poma, suoque dilecto reddit, quae maligni spiritus furari concupiscunt.



## CAPUT VIII

« Quis mihi det te fratrem meum sugentem ubera matris meae. » Quis, inquit, hoc mihi det, quis hunc honorem, hanc dignitatem, hanc beatitudinem mihi tribuat, ut tu summi regis Filius carnem sumens homo fias, et meus frater appelleris, ipseque proprio ore dicas: « Narrabo nomen tuum fratribus meis [n: (Psal. XXI, 23)]. » Matris autem Synagogae ubera elicuit Christus, quoniam legis et prophetarum mandata ipse adimplevit; sive etiam quia secundum carnem, sicut scriptum est, et « aetate et sapientia proficiebat coram Deo, et hominibus [n: (Luc. II, 52)]. » [1282B] -- « Et inveniam te foris: » inquit, ideo dixit, te foris inveniam, te in homine videam, a Patre procedas, in mundum venias, et gentibus manifesteris. « Et deosculer te. » Hoc autem est quod in capite hujus libri scriptum est. « Osculetur me osculo oris sui. » -- « Nemo me despiciat. » Tu me, inquit, dilexisti, pro me carnem assumpsisti, nemo me despiciat; quandoquidem tanto viro sum desponsata. « Apprehendam te, et ducam in domum matris meae. » Confirmatio. « Et in cubiculum genitricis meae. » Apprehendit enim, quoniam pio amore ei inhaeret. Duxit autem in domum matris suae, in carnem videlicet, quae de terra universali matre facta est. Pro Ecclesiae namque dilectione *631* Christus Dominus noster homo fieri voluit. « Ibi me docebis. » In hac, [1282C] inquit, domo, in hoc tabernaculo, in hoc loco dormitionis et mortis, me docebis, per quam viam et doctrinam ad te venire valeam. Merito autem Christi humanitas cubiculum dicitur; siquidem ibi dormire visus est, quod secundum divinitatem nec dormire, nec mori potest. « Et dabo tibi poculum ex vino condito. » Primitiva namque vinea in amaritudinem conversa, cum uvas dare debuisset, labruscas fecit. Ecclesia vero vinum dat bene conditum, Deo delectabile, et ad bibendum suave. Sed quare conditum nisi quia litterae spiritualis intelligentia admiscetur. Vinum namque conditum dabat Paulus; quoniam sicut in vino pigmentato quis delectatur, ita in ipsius sana doctrina suavique praedicatione [1282D] delectabatur Christus. Vinum namque conditum dabat, quando ad Dei laudem et honorem inter perfectos sapientiam praedicabat. « Et mustum malorum granatorum meorum. » Mustum enim novum esse vinum [1283A] nemo dubitat; quod quidem ebullire non cessat, donec totum purgatum fuerit. Mala vero granata apostoli, caeterique martyres sunt. Horum autem mustum, horum novum canticum fervere distulit, donec et haereticorum error, et paganorum infidelitas cessavit. Dabat igitur Ecclesia malorum granatorum mustum, quando Christi martyres et Novum Testamentum praedicabant, et proprio sanguine infundebant.

« Laeva ejus sub capite meo, et dextra illius amplexabitur me. » Vox Christi: « Adjuro vos, filiae Jerusalem, ne suscitetis, neque evigilare faciatis dilectam, quoadusque ipsa velit. » Per capreas, [1283D] inquit, et cervos, per apostolos et doctores, per virtutes, et fidem, et bonam operationem, quibus ad promissum bravium curritis, et serpentum venena superatis. Haec autem, quia superius exposita sunt, ulterius expositione non indigent. Synagoga de Ecclesia: « Quae est ista, quae ascendit de deserto, [1284A] deliciis affluens, et innixa super dilectum suum? » Quae, inquit, qualis, quam pulchra, quam fortis est ista, quae semper ascendit, semper ad altiora festinat, nunquam descendit, sed virtutum gradibus coelestia petit? Sed unde venit? « De deserto, » de terra invia et inaquosa, et quondam a Deo derelicta. Sed quomodo venit? « Affluens deliciis, » copiosa virtutibus, cum plenis lampadibus. Quis eam portat? Sequitur: « Innixa super dilectem suum, » ei conjuncta, ei adhaerens, quem tota mente, cunctisque viribus dilexit, quique post se eam trahere promisit. Vox sponsi ad sponsam: « Sub arbore malo suscitavi te. » Mortua, inquit, eras, in peccatis jacebas; sed ego carnem sumens sub arbore mali resuscitavi. De hoc autem [1284B] malo superius dicitur: « Sicut malum inter ligna silvarum, sic dilectus meus inter filios. » Haec autem arbor, haec caro nostri Salvatoris eos obumbrat, quos suscitavit. Potest autem et de cruce hoc intelligi, quae ob Christi sanguinem hujus pomi colorem et speciem habuit. « Ibi corrupta est mater tua, » Synagoga videlicet, quae Christum Dominum crucifixit: secundum illud: « Corrupti et abominabiles facti sunt [n: (Psal. XIII, 1)]. » -- « Ibi violata est genitrix tua, » quia legitimum sponsum dereliquit. Ecclesia ad Christum dicit: « Pone me ut signaculum super cor tuum, ut signaculum super brachium tuum. » Christus enim et signaculum, et clavis, firmumque sigillum est cordis sanctorum. Non possunt sanctorum corpora frangi, *632* non [1284C] possunt eorum secreta violari, tanto et tam munita sigillo. Signum fecimus, amici recordemur. Nobis Christus fidem dedit, signum et pignus amoris. Super brachium hoc signum portant, qui omnia quae faciunt, in nomine Domini faciunt. Signaculum est in corde, signaculum est in manu, quoniam et in cogitationibus, et in operibus semper Christi memores sunt sancti. Sit igitur Christus nostri cordis signum et doctor, ut ejus signo, et admonitioni facile credamus. « Quia fortis est ut mors dilectio. » -- « Perfecta namque charitas foras mittit timorem [n: (Joan. IV, 17)]. » Non timet dilectio mortem, non superatur amore. Fortis est mors, fortis est dilectio. Non timent Christi discipuli mortem, quoniam eorum dilectio fortis est ut mors. [1284D] Cum morte pugnant, morti occurrunt. Recordantur enim, et signaculum habent, quoniam Domini dilectio super eos firmissima fuit. Pater enim « proprio Filio non pepercit, sed pro nobis omnibus illum morti tradidit [n: (Rom. VIII, 32)]. » Filius autem per Prophetam dicit: « Zelus domus tuae comedit me [1285A] [n: (Psal. LXVI, 10)]. » Confirmatio: « Dura sicut infernus aemulatio. » De hac aemulatione Apostolus ait: « Aemulor enim vos Dei aemulatione [n: (II Cor. XI, 2)]. » Infernus omnia domat, charitas omnia superat. Non timet charitas infernum, non timet ejus principes et habitatores. Metonymia est. « Lampades ejus lampades ignis, atque flammarum. » Semper enim infernus igne ardet inexstinguibili. Semper charitas igne accenditur insuperabili. De hoc autem igne Dominus ait: « Ignem veni mittere in terram [n: (Luc. XII, 49)]. » Hic autem ignis vitia exurit, et corda illuminat. « Aquae multae non potuerunt exstinguere charitatem. » Merito igitur inferno charitas assimilatur; siquidem ejus ignis, sicut illius inexstinguibilis est. « Nec flumina obruent illam. » Nam sicut Apostolus [1285B] ait [n: (Rom. VIII, 35)], nec tribulatio, nec augustia, nec mors, nec vita, neque ulla persecutio a charitate, quae est in Christo Jesu, sanctos separare poterit. « Si dederit homo omnem substantiam domus suae pro dilectione, quasi nihil despiciet eam. » Quid, inquit, de charitate dicam? Quibus eam laudibus exaltabo? Major est quam cogitari, major est quam dici possit. Quod pretium charitati, quae divinae comparatur dilectioni? Non despicias charitatem, non eam divitiis comparari posse dicas. Nam si omnia quae habes, dederis, si omnem substantiam domus tuae pro dilectione distribueris, et his te charitatem emisse putaveris, despicis charitatem, quae vendi non potest. In pretium ponis, cui pretium non est. Omne namque pretium supercellit. Fugiunt divitiae, [1285C] remanent amici, fortuna te fallit, amici pro te moriuntur. Quaeramus igitur illum amicum qui nunquam moritur, nunquam amicos deserit, nunquam mentitur, omnibus abundat; qui amicitiam laudans, inquit: « Majorem hac dilectionem nemo habet, quam ut animam suam ponat quis pro amicis suis [n: (Joan. XV, 13)]. » Moriens igitur pro nobis hanc complevit dilectionem.

## CAPUT VIII (cont.)


Christus ad Synagogam de Ecclesia: « Soror nostra parva, et ubera non habet. » Soror ista Ecclesia gentium intelligitur. Dicunt ergo apostoli, dicunt Domini nuntii, legati sumus; Domino nostro uxorem quaerimus. Quam igitur ei dabimus? Soror nostra parva est, nuper genita, insipiens et indocta. Ubera non habet: Testamenta non videt, nondum parere, nondum filios enutrire [1286B] potest, virum nescit. Alloquenda est igitur, et de nuptiis admonenda. Sed « quid faciemus sorori nostrae in die, quando alloquenda est? » Quibus verbis, quibusve promissis ejus animum temperabimus. Sequitur: « Si murus est, aedificemus super eum propugnacula argentea. » Si, inquit, murum, constantiam, fidem et fortitudinem in ea reperiemus, super eum propugnacula argentea et divina eloquia aedificemus. Prophetarum namque sententiae, doctorumque sermones muro et fidei nostrae propugnacula sunt; quoniam his defendimur, his vitia superamus, his haereticis resistimus. Haec *633* autem argentea dicuntur, quoniam nihil plumbi, vel aeris, nihilque falsitatis in eis reperitur, « Si ostium est, compingamus illud tabulis cedrinis, » [1286C] etc. Ostium, inquit, pingamus, portas signemus, et variemus, variemus, ut Dei exercitus, virtutumque multitudo introitum inveniant; signum recognoscant, et in decoris ornatibus delectentur. Sive etiam compingamus et claudamus, ut undique portae compactae nulla ex parte vitia ingredi possint. Haec autem cedrinis tabulis, exemplis propheticis, immarcessibilibus, aliisque sententiis muniantur. Vox Ecclesiae: « Et ubera mea sicut turris. » Ego, inquit, murus sum, fortis sum, constans sum, vitiis resisto, inimicos expugno. « Et ubera mea sicut turris. » Ubera, inquit, mea, doctrina et sapientia mea turris sunt. Alta est doctrina, grandis est sapientia, bene munita, bene armata, non haereticorum, [1286D] non philosophorum sophismata timens. Haec enim ubera filios nutriunt et defendunt. Unde et turris et ubera vocantur. Sed ex quo tempore talis est fortitudo? Sequitur: « Ex quo facta est coram eo quasi pacem reperiens; » id est ex quo Christus me dilexit, Patrique reconciliavit; ex quo angelica tuba cecinit; « Gloria in excelsis Deo, et in terra pax hominibus bonae voluntatis [n: (Luc. II, 14)]. » Synagoga Ecclesiae dicit: « Vinea fuit pacifico, quae habet populos. » Per vineam Ecclesiam; pro pacifico vero Christum intelligas. « Vinea enim Domini exercituum, domus Israel est [n: (Isa. V, 7)]. » -- « Ipse [1287A] autem est pax nostra, quae fecit utraque unum [n: (Ephes. II, 14)]. » Haec autem vinea populos habet, quia Judaeos et gentiles, Graecos et barbaros omnesque nationes in unum colligit. « Tradidit eam custodibus, » id est apostolis et doctoribus, qui eam colerent, et amputarent, et a furibus custodirent. « Vir affert pro fructu ejus mille argenteos. » Millenarius namque numerus pro summa perfectione et plenitudine ponitur. Et tale est ac si diceret: Vir sanctus et catholicus ut hujus vineae fruatur merito et beatitudine, omnia tribuit quaecunque possidet. Christus dicit: « Vinea mea coram me est. » Vinea, inquit, mea, haereditas, vel Ecclesia mea coram me est, mihique servit, et quamvis custodibus eam tradidissem, semper tamen praesens [1287B] adsum, qui eam munio, praeparo, et custodio. « Mille tui pacifici, » subauditur, tibi servantur. Quos autem superius argenteos dixit, pacificos hic appellat. Sed quare pacificos? Quoniam Deo nos conciliant, ejus inimicitiam, iram et indignationem mitigant, nobisque pacem praeparant, et in pacem nos inducunt. Hi autem Ecclesiae reservantur, eique multiplicati reddentur. « Et ducenti his qui custodiunt fructus ejus. » Ducenti, inquit, millium pacificorum servantur apostolis et doctoribus. His enim sicuti regibus et magistris duplex honor est habendus; siquidem caeteros custodiunt, et pro caeteris [1288A] vigilant et moriuntur. Christus Ecclesiae dicit: « Quae habitas in hortis, amici auscultant. » Tu, inquit, Ecclesia in hortis habitas, in liliis delectaris, inter rosas et violas jaces, undique flores, undique virtutes, undique doctorum sententiae sunt. « Fulcite me floribus, » dixisti; completa est petitio tua. Te mei amici, videlicet angeli et apostoli, auscultant, quid credas, quam spem habeas, ad quem finem tendas audire desiderant. « Fac me audire vocem tuam; » laudem scilicet, jubilationem, canticum laudis et confessionis. Vox Ecclesiae ad Christum: « Fuge, dilecte mi, assimilare capreae, hinnuloque cervorum super montes aromatum. » Fuge, inquit, relinque terras, advola ad Patrem, ut qui te hominem tantum putant, verum Deum esse credant. [1288B] Propter me venisti, domum meam intrasti; jam me osculatus es; tibi sum conjuncta, tibi desponsata. Revertere igitur, trahe me post te, redde vicem, in domum tuam me introducas. « Assimilare capreae, » pete montes, pete coelos, pete superiora; « hinnuloque cervorum, » ut in umbra, in Selmon, et in refrigerio habites; super montes aromatum in aeternum maneas, ubi odor est suavissimus, locus delectabilis, splendor ineffabilis, copia inenarrabilis; ibi sancti exsultant, ibi angeli laetantur; ibi cum Patre et Spiritu sancto laus, honor et gloria in aeternum tibi cantatur. Amen.

## Exposition on the Song of Songs

[1233] *605*

## CHAPTER ONE.

[1233C]

« Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth. » The voice of the aforesaid woman.

[1234C]Many things, she says, you have often announced to me, O envoys of the heavenly King; many things concerning his nobility, his riches, his strength, his beauty, and many things concerning the man's wisdom [1235A] you have reported. I have seen Moses, I have seen Elias, I have seen Jeremias, I have seen David, and I have seen others too, who announced his coming to me. I believe their words, I languish with love, I am ready; let the envoys cease. Now let him come himself, let him be made manifest, let him fasten kisses upon me, let him give embraces, and let him speak to me with his own mouth. Apostrophe. Thee, she says, I love, and I desire; I long to hear thee, to see thee. Why so? « Because thy breasts are better than wine. » Moses gave me wine, the rest of the prophets gave me wine — bitter and strong, harsh and rough to drink. For the words of the prophets are hard, not only to do, but even to speak. For, to say nothing of uttering and pronouncing them, in certain places they can scarcely be understood. But the preaching of Christ turned the wine into milk. For the two breasts are the two testaments, [1235B] from which Christ, by teaching and expounding, drew back a milky and sweet suavity. For those whom the law looked to slay, he mercifully healed. For the Jews wished to stone the woman taken in adultery, but Christ said, « Neither will I condemn thee [n: (Joan. VII, 10)]. » And these words are better than wine. « Fragrant with the finest ointments. » What is signified by the ointment, if not the sevenfold grace of the Holy Spirit? And with these both the New and the Old Testament are fragrant, and shine, and give forth their scent. This odor the preaching of Christ brought in, since it made some wise, others understanding, others strong, others devout. « And the odor of thy ointments is above all spices. » By the spices we understand whatever things are odor-bearing. But what could be of so great an odor and so great a sweetness that it might be the Spirit himself, filled with whom the Apostle said: [1235C] « We are the good odor of Christ unto God? » [n: (II Cor. II, 15.)] The voice of the Church to Christ: « Thy name is as ointment poured out. » Thy name, she says, like ointment poured out, has furnished health to all that believe. For Christ is named from the chrism, in which name we are all called Christians, cleansed by the water of baptism. This name, therefore, poured out over the elect, has joined them together by the grace of the Holy Spirit. « Therefore the young maidens have loved thee. » By the young maidens are understood the primitive and new churches, which, lately born to God and baptized, were frail after the manner of women, and [1236A] had brought forth not many children. But she, having left behind her former oldness and received the Holy Spirit, had loved Christ with all her strength and with every affection of motherhood. The voice of the Church to Christ:

« Draw me after thee. » For Christ draws after himself whoever imitate him, so that they who are exalted above the heavens by his own command: « No man hath ascended into heaven, but he that descended from heaven [n: (Joan. III, 13)]. » He indeed ascended by himself, who is both perfect *606* God and perfect man. But the rest, since they cannot ascend by themselves, must needs be drawn. They are drawn, therefore, as the Lord himself says: « When I shall be lifted up from the earth, I will draw all things to myself [n: (ibid. XII, 32)]. » -- « And we will run after the odor of thy ointments, » that is, in the sweetness [1236B] of virtues, of preachings, and of graces. For those run after the odor of these who, captivated by their sweetness and delight, work good things without ceasing. But those who stink with vices — to them indeed all these things give no fragrance. The voice of the bride to the young maidens: « The King hath brought me into his storerooms. » Change of person. Already, she says, the King of kings has brought me by faith and hope into his storerooms and into the eternal tabernacles. We may also understand by the storerooms the several books of the prophets, into which the Church, being brought in, is made drunk with spiritual wine. Whence the Psalmist: « They shall be inebriated with the plenty of thy house [n: (Psal. XXXV, 9)]. » Apostrophe. « We will exult and rejoice in thee. » For when churchly men find the praises and the mighty works of God in the sacred volumes, they exult and rejoice in so great and such a [1236C] man. And at last, when they have come to that highest blessedness, having received the highest and eternal goods, they will exult in him alone. « Mindful of thy breasts above wine. » In thee, she says, we will exult, mindful of thy breasts coming above the wine. The milk came above the wine, the New Testament came above the Old; the wine was tempered, and the law was made sweet, mild, and intelligible. The New Testament, therefore, was consummated over the house of Israel and over the house of Juda. « The kings love thee. » For he who rules himself and others is by a true definition called a king. For the apostles, the bishops, and the priests are kings. And unless the apostles had loved Christ, [1237A] they would not indeed have died for him. Therefore kings and upright men love him from whom they are made kings and upright. The voice of the synagogue: « I am black, but comely, O daughters of Jerusalem. » She called herself black for the ignobility of her race, but comely on account of penance and faith. And it is the Church of the Gentiles, or the apostolic company, that says this. You, she says, are daughters of Jerusalem, daughters of Libanus, daughters of whitening. But I was the daughter of Cedar, the daughter of darkness, the daughter of stags. I am the people that sat in darkness. I am she to whom it was said: « Ye were sometime darkness [n: (Ephes. V, 8)]. » I grant, therefore, that I am black, since I was born in sins: black according to my creation and my former life, but according to my regeneration made whiter than snow. « I am comely; » but [1237B] where comely? In my eyes, in my ears, and in all my members. For eyes are uncomely in that they long to see uncomely and base things; ears are uncomely in that they delight to hear vain talk and buffoonery. But on the contrary, « how fair are the feet of them that preach peace, of them that preach good things [n: (Rom. X, 15)]! » I am black without, but most beautiful and comely within. She seems black to man, in that which he sees; most beautiful, in that which lies hidden from man. For man considers the face, but God the hearts.

« As the tabernacles of Cedar. » Cedar is interpreted *darkness*. But the blackness of darkness is put to flight by light alone. The Church, then, was black as the tabernacles of Cedar, and being illumined by the sun of justice she was made white. Whence the Evangelist: « And the light, he says, shineth in darkness, [1237C] and the darkness did not comprehend it [n: (Joan. I, 5)]. » The tabernacles of Cedar are indeed those in which the princes of darkness dwell. And in short, according to the flesh the just are of no greater beauty than the unjust. « As the skins of Solomon. » I am black, she says, as the tabernacles of Cedar, but comely as the skins of Solomon. Let not Solomon therefore despise me, since my skin agrees with his skin. The Church, then, is fair and comely among women, since indeed the aforesaid Solomon « is fair in form above the sons of men [n: (Psal. XLIV, 3)]. » The voice of the Church: « Consider not that I am swarthy. » And this is said in the person of the apostles. I am swarthy, she says, and as to my outward form I am uncomely; not anointed, not plump, not [1237D] dainty, but rather rough and hard to look upon. Yet let no one despise these things, but let him ponder more subtly what lies within. » Because the sun hath discolored me. » I have not rested in the shade, I have not given myself over to idleness upon a bed. [1238A] What then? I labored in the vineyard, I tilled the field, I kept watch, I fasted; and moreover, having endured many adversities under the sun, I have been discolored and made swarthy. What wonder? The voice of the Synagogue: « For the sons of my mother have fought against me. » There was for me, she says, opportunity of rest, since it was necessary to prepare what was needful and *607* to fight against enemies. For not only barbarians, but even the sons of my mother made war upon me. Without, therefore, were fightings; within, fears; on this side the sword of tyrants, on that the disputation of the Jews and of the heretics. You may understand her mother to be Judaea, or the synagogue. Whence the Apostle: « When, he says, it pleased him who separated me from my mother's womb [n: (Galat. I, 15)], » etc. But we may also understand by this mother iniquity. Whence the Psalmist: [1238B] « For I was conceived in iniquities, and in sins did my mother conceive me [n: (Ps. L, 7)]; » she says:

« The sons of my mother have fought against me. » That is, the passions of the body have assailed me, the allurements of the flesh have discolored me, and therefore the sun of justice has not shone upon me.



## CHAPTER ONE. (cont.)

« They have set me a keeper in the vineyards. » Who, then, sets keepers in the vineyards, except to ward off thieves? God planted one vineyard, and because it was turned into bitterness, many other vineyards were planted. Whence also that saying: « And they sowed fields, and planted vineyards [n: (Ps. CVI, 37)]. » In these the apostles were set as keepers, lest all they that pass by the way should gather her vintage. « My vineyard I have not kept. » One vineyard, she says, I have left, but many [1238C] vineyards I have kept. And the many vineyards are the many churches. But the synagogue is one. And the apostles left her, as it is written: « To you it behooved us first to speak the word of God; but because you have rejected it, and have judged yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold, we turn to the Gentiles [n: (Act. XIII, 46)]. » This can also be read as a question. Have I not kept my vineyard? I have indeed kept it. And in that he set the vineyard first in the plural and then in the singular, he figured the unity of the Church, which, however much it be divided according to the character of places, is nevertheless one in faith and love. And the apostles and the doctors kept it, lest Arius, Sabellius, and the other thieves should craftily steal away some cluster, or separate any of the faithful from the Church. The voice of the Church [1238D] to Christ: « Show me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou liest down at midday. » Show me, she says, make me to know and firmly to understand, O shepherd, O ruler, whom with my whole mind and with all my strength [1239A] I have loved and do love; show me where thou feedest thy flock, in what place, and with what food thou nourishest thy sheep. For God's sheep are fed in the assembly of preaching and in the sacred volumes. And this has been shown also to those bishops who, being dumb dogs unable to bark, suffer God's animals to perish of hunger. « Where thou liest down at midday. » What is meant by midday, if not the too greatly burning affliction of the saints? Say, she says, say, O shepherd, where thou liest down at midday, where thou art when the saints are afflicted, where thou art when thy lambs are torn in pieces by wolves? Art thou not he who, as a good shepherd, layest down thy life for the sheep? The heat is heavy, the sheep thirst, they are burned with the warmth. Lead them to the harbor, lead them to the shade. I know; thou wilt say: I am in thee, in thee I lie down and rest. « For upon whom doth my spirit [1239B] rest, but upon the humble, and the quiet, and him that trembleth at my words? » [n: (Isa, LVI, 2.)] And likewise: « Know you not that you are the temple of God, and that the Holy Spirit dwelleth in you? » [n: (Cor. III, 16.)] Why then am I troubled? I know, thou wilt say, because through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdoms of heaven. The answer is true; now I fear nothing, since so great a guest guards the city. I do not shudder at the heat, since the living fountain is with me. There follows: « Lest I begin to wander after the flocks of thy companions. » What is meant by the companions, if not heretics and philosophers? But why companions? Because they too are shepherds, and feed a flock. And through their flocks and their conventicles those men wander who know not the way of the true pasture [1239C] and of the divine meadow. Let us ask our Lord, therefore, both to show us the sheepfold, and by his mercy to set us in a place of pasture.

Likewise verses: Why shouldst thou read me so many prophets, O royal Bridegroom?
Let the envoys cease, who are ready only to give words.
Thee I desire, thee I believe, thee alone I seek to look upon.
Now have mercy on me, now suffer thyself to be seen.
And now let it be thy care to give kisses to thy bride,
And to our ears the strains of thy sweet voice.
Now let it sound forth, I beg thee, if there be any love of thine toward me.


The voice of Christ to the Church: « If thou know not thyself, O most beautiful among women, go forth. » If thou, he says, most beautiful of women, fair of form, knowest not thyself; if, forgetful of thyself, unmindful of thy nobility, go forth, depart, *608* [1239D] and wander, as thou hast said, after the tracks of the flocks. Follow the heretics, imitate the philosophers. For we know not our own selves, when, forgetful of our dignity, of our baptism, and of our newness, we are made subject to error and to vanity, and follow the tracks of the flocks of [1240A] [sic: *caparrum*] and of he-goats.

« And feed thy kids beside the tabernacles of the shepherds. » if thou, he says, shalt not have known thyself, and shalt have departed from me, thy lambs will soon become kids. For just as in baptism roes are turned into lambs, so, by sinning and departing from God, we turn pure souls and most gentle lambs into butting and stinking he-goats. And these kids, beside the tabernacles of the shepherds and the conventicles of the heretics, having scorned the sweet food of the Scriptures, are fed with poisonous grass, that is, they drink in depraved teachings. The voice of Christ: « To my cavalry among the chariots of Pharao have I likened thee, my friend. » Neither ought thou, he says, to leave me nor to forget thyself. For I have likened thee to my cavalry among the chariots of Pharao And the [sic: *Eeclesia*] is likened to it for this reason, namely, [1240B] that the chariots and horsemen of Pharao pursued the people of Israel. But as Pharao, pursuing the aforesaid people with chariots and horsemen, was drowned in the sea, so also the devil, lying in wait with a multitude of vices for the souls of men, perishes in baptism. Having therefore received so great a benefit, let no one forget himself or God. The young maidens to the bride:

« Thy cheeks are beautiful as the turtledove's. » But when she had heard these words, as it were of rebuke, on account of the words spoken above, she drew upon herself the blush of shame. For she had said, « lest I begin to wander. » For wandering belongs to harlots. Recalling therefore this word and this rashness, she blushed. But the Bridegroom, when he saw this, [1240C] praised her virginal modesty. For he says: « Thy cheeks are beautiful, » — thy face is bashful and chaste. Thou blushest to speak, or to have done, or even to have thought base things. For thou art not of those women who take their strength from crime. But how beautiful? As the turtledove's, as a virgin's, as of one who keeps great chastity and conjugal faith. For the Church serves no husband but one. « Thy neck as necklaces. » As the other virgins, he says, delight in necklaces, so thou delightest in the beauty of thy neck alone. What is meant by the neck, if not the doctors? For through the neck food is sent down into the belly, and out of it words also come forth. But the Church is nourished and instructed by the doctors. The office of the neck, therefore, is fulfilled by the doctors. Moreover, the weakness of the neck is the ruin of the whole body. The voice of the friends: « Golden [1240D] *murenulae* will we make thee. » *Murenulae* indeed are ornaments of a virgin's neck, so named from the fish *murena*. And they signify the discourses of the prophets, lengthy, and [sic: *dictinctos*], and praiseworthy. *Murenulae* [1241A] were made for us by Moses, Isaias, Jeremias, David, and by him indeed who wrote these things, Ecclesiastes. « Inlaid with silver. » They are *murenulae* indeed, because they are slippery; but golden, because they shine forth with the light of wisdom; and they are said to be inlaid with silver, because they are marked out by the purity of eloquence.

Verses: Blessed Virgin,
Made wondrous,
Chaste bride,
Sweet friend;
Thee wisely,
And becomingly,
In order I fashion.
Risen in thy ways,
Pleasing to my
Disciples,
Know thou the pastures:
And come thou to them,
Much peace be to thee,
And all things safe.
What pleases the One,
Is grievous to none.


[1241B]The voice of the bride: « While the king was at his repose, my nard gave forth its odor. » While my king, she says, my bridegroom, my beloved, was at his repose, upon the little bed of the flesh, in the humanity which he took from a virginal womb, « my nard gave forth its odor. » And this can be understood according to the letter of Mary, who poured out the alabaster box of ointment upon the head of him as he reclined. For straightway the whole house was filled with the odor of the ointment. But spiritually it is understood of the Church. For before our Savior had come in man, the nard gave forth its odor in few, since the virtues and prayers of few were pleasing to the Lord. But after he came in the flesh, and the Lord went forth as a bridegroom out of his chamber, [1241C] straightway the virtues and prayers of the saints gave forth their odor. Whence the Apostle: « We are, he says, a good odor unto God [n: (II Cor. II, 15)]. » And the Psalmist: « Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight [n: (Ps. CXL)]. » Hence it is that John saw golden vials full of odors [n: (Apoc. V, 8)]. For after the incarnation of Christ both the virtue of the saints and their number increased. The nard therefore gave *609* forth its odor to Christ the Lord when he was made flesh. « A bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me. » He set myrrh for bitterness. For Christ was to the Church a bundle of myrrh, and indeed a gathering of great grief and great bitterness. For how could she be otherwise than in grief and bitterness, widowed of so great and such a husband? So too it can [1241D] be said: « My beloved is to me. » For my sake and for my profit was he made a bundle of myrrh, since he submitted himself for me to death and to the bitterness of the passion. Was he not carrying a bundle of myrrh [1242A] and of bitterness when he said: « My soul is sorrowful even unto death? « [n: (Matth. XXVI, 38.)] He was indeed a bundle, because he both drew many to himself and slew many with himself. For all the martyrs are gathered, as it were into one bundle, for his death. « He shall abide between my breasts. » For the excellent Bridegroom abides between the breasts of the bride, since he is not separated from her memory and her embrace. For the place of the heart is between the breasts. And where the heart is, there also is the memory. He therefore who abides between the breasts, since he lies in the heart, cannot escape the memory. Happy is that soul, and exceedingly happy, between whose breasts Christ abides, in whose heart he lies, and who never forgets him. « My beloved is to me a cluster of Cyprus. » For the wine of the island of Cyprus is the best [1242B]. And wine gladdens the heart of man. And Christ is to his saints a cluster of Cyprus, since they are gladdened by the draught of his blood. And in short, if wine signifies gladness, then he who had been a bundle of myrrh in dying is rightly called a cluster of Cyprus in rising again. Whence the Psalmist: « In the evening, he says, weeping shall tarry, and in the morning gladness [n: (Psal. XXIX, 6)]. » He is therefore a cluster of Cyprus. Where? There follows: « In the vineyards of Engaddi. » Engaddi is interpreted *the fountain of the kid*. And the fountain of the kid is in the churches. And the churches are the vineyards of Engaddi. For the fountain of baptism is in the Church, and he who enters it is a kid, but he who comes out is a lamb.

Verses of Scir Hascirim. [1242C]The Lord, who made all things, deigning to take flesh,
of his own will redeemed by death the ruin of the human race:
Hanging on the cross, when he suffered, a bundle of myrrh
believe that he was. For he said sorrowful with death.
Moreover Peter also wept bitterly; but afterwards the nard gave forth
its odor, when he sought the heavens in a bloodstained garment.



## CHAPTER ONE. (cont.)


The voice of Christ: « Behold, thou art beautiful, my friend. » Confirmation. « Behold, thou art beautiful. » Thou art beautiful, he says, thou art without spot, thou art chaste within and without. For great is the friendship between Christ and the Church, since both Christ would not hesitate to die for the [sic: *Ecelesia*], and the Church for Christ: « For greater love than this no man hath, than that a man lay down his life for his friends [n: (Joan. XV, 13)]. » The voice [1242D] of the Church: « Thy eyes are those of doves. » Thine eyes, he says — thy memory, thy understanding, and thy reason — are those of doves, that is, chaste and simple. For in no way art thou proud of understanding or of wisdom. For thou art not of those [1243A] who say: « Our lips are our own [n: (Psal. XI, 5)]. » The voice of the Church, or of Christ: « Behold, thou art beautiful, my friend, and comely. » For in this the greatest concord of them both is proved, that each of the two indeed praises the other for beauty. His comeliness and beauty can neither be spoken nor even conceived. « Our little bed is flowery. » What is meant by the little bed, if not the heart? Whence the Lord himself says: « Enter into thy chamber [n: (Matth. VI)]. » And this little bed is flowery with virtues and with purity of conscience. And we may understand by this little bed also that blessedness of the saints, in which, resting in perpetual quiet and repose, the just shall flourish like the palm tree. « The beams of our houses are of cedar, our panelled ceilings of cypress. » And these houses you may understand to be the churches, dispersed throughout this world. And in them [1243B] both the summit and the foundation is Christ, since by him they are upheld. But the columns and the walls are the apostles and the prophets. And the beams are the prelates and the doctors, by whom they are ruled, upheld, and covered. But the panelled ceilings, which pertain more to adornment than to usefulness, are the virgins and the widows, together with the order of monks. For the more these are divided from the world, the more do they shine with virtues and with holiness. And these profit themselves, and are no hindrance to the rest. But why are the one said to be of cedar and the other of cypress? For the cedar and the cypress are of an unfading and fragrant nature. And the saints are both immortal, and an odor most sweet to the Lord. *610*



## CHAPTER II.

The voice of Christ: « I am the flower of the field. » He does not indeed deny that he [1243C] is beautiful and comely, but rather affirms that he is the flower and the beauty and the honor of the whole world. He is moreover the flower of the field, that is, the son of that virgin and unplowed earth of which it is written: « And our earth shall yield her fruit [n: (Psal. LXV, 7)]. » Whence Isaias: « There shall come forth, he says, a rod out of the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise up out of his root [n: (Isa. XI, 1)]. » -- « And the lily of the valleys. » For this lily is not of the mountains but of the valleys, since the Lord loves not the proud but the humble. As he himself says: « Learn of me, because I am meek and humble of heart [n: (Matth. XI, 29)]. » The lily is born in the valley; the Savior dwells in the heart of the humble. « As the lily among thorns, so is my friend among the daughters. » For the lily [1243D] among thorns is pricked and pressed, yet it grows and gives forth its odor. And so the Church too is many times afflicted, oppressed, and pricked by her daughters — namely by heretics and schismatics, whom she has borne in the font of baptism. And this according to the letter. But spiritually [1244A] the lily among thorns is Christ among the Jews, and the just man among sinners. By thorns indeed the lily is oppressed, and by the Jews Christ is afflicted, wounded, and crucified. Among thorns the lily grows, since Christ reigns from the tree. And this lily upon the cross gave forth a most sweet odor to the Father. Whence the Psalmist: « Let my prayer, he says, be directed as incense in thy sight; the lifting up of my hands as the evening sacrifice [n: (Psal. CXL, 2)]. » And the primitive and apostolic Church, among the innumerable daughters whom she bore, holds this fitting likeness. Let but one city assemble, nay two, or four, and a whole province. Let Peter be set in the midst, let Paul be said to be present — does he not seem to thee a lily among thorns, a most pleasing flower [1244B] among briers?

Verses: I am the flower of the field, the glory and praise of the kindly order;
The angelic company is subject to me;
I embrace all things, heaven, beyond the level of the sea:
The Lord of all, Father and God —
Who but I alone? No one, I tell thee, no one.


The voice of the Church: « As the apple tree among the trees of the woods, so is my beloved among the sons. » For as the apple tree is fruitful among unfruitful trees, so was Christ among the Jews, and once among the apostles too. For this is that tree of which it is said that « it shall bring forth its fruit in due season [n: (Psal. I, 3)]. » For at that time the apostles were without fruit, while Christ was yielding many fruits in Judaea. And in comparison with him [1244C] they seemed not only without fruit, but even dry. Whence he himself says: « If in the green wood they do these things, what shall be done in the dry? » [n: (Luc. XXIII, 31.)] But how great a fertility these men, who before were dry and unfruitful, would bear once they had tasted the apples of this tree and received the Holy Spirit, is gathered from the words of the Savior himself, who says: « That you should go, and should bring forth fruit, and your fruit should remain [n: (Joan. XV, 16)]. » -- « I sat down under his shadow, whom I had desired; » that is, at last I rested in his protection. For the Church was black, and darkened by the heat of vices, when she fled to the shade of this tree, when she came to know its shadow and felt the cooling of its heat.

« And his fruit was sweet to my throat. » Under his shadow, [1244D] she says, I sat down, I came to know the fruits of this tree, and I was refreshed in the contemplation of him, and filled with sweet sayings. For of these fruits the Church says also elsewhere: « How sweet are thy words to my palate, above honey to my mouth [n: (Psal. CXVIII, 103)]! » -- « The king brought [1245A] me into the wine cellar. » What is meant by the wine cellar, if not the teaching of the New and Old Testament? For of this cellar it is said: « For in the hand of the Lord there is a cup of pure wine full of mixture [n: (Psal. LXXIV, 9)]. » For drunk with the wine of this cellar the Apostle said: « We speak wisdom among the perfect [n: (I Cor. II, 6)]. » And the Psalmist: « And thy cup, he says, which inebriateth, how goodly is it! » [n: (Psal. XXII, 5.)] And the Church, brought into this cellar, is made drunk with the sweetness of the wine from on high. « He set charity in order within me. » How is charity set in order in this cellar? Wilt thou hear? « Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with thy whole heart, and with thy whole mind, and with all thy strength [n: (Matth. XXII, 37)]. » What further? « And thy neighbor as thyself [n: (ibid., 39)]. » This is the order and the true rule [1245B] of charity, that we love both God above all things, and our neighbor as ourselves. He set it in order in the first cellar; he set it in order in the second also. And in the first *611* how? « Thou shalt love thy neighbor, and shalt hate thy enemy [n: (Matth. V, 43)]. » What is said in the second? « Love your enemies, do good to them that hate you [n: (ibid., 44)]. » Does this order seem to thee contrary? Not contrary at all, but rather fitting; otherwise it would not be an order. For what in the first is understood of vice, in the second is understood of nature, so that it is said thus: Thou shalt hate thy enemy — the vice, not the nature. Thou shalt love thy enemy — the nature, not the vice. « Stay me up with flowers, compass me about with apples, because I languish with love. » For the bride desires to be stayed up with flowers and with pomegranates, that she may rest upon them [1245C]. The charity of the Bridegroom, she says, is already set in order within me. I love, I languish with love. You therefore, my servants, my faithful ones, my clients, my confidants, my intimates, stay me up with flowers, compass me about with apples. For the apostles and the doctors stay up the Church with flowers, and compass her about indeed with apples. For many flowers Gregory, and many Ambrose, Jerome, and Augustine brought to the Church. By the flowers we understand sentences; by the apples, believers. We may also understand by the flowers the beginning of a work, and by the apples its perfection. For the flowers become fruits when the hearers believe the sentences, and fulfill in deed what they believe. « His left hand is under my head, and his right hand shall embrace me. » For when Christ died for the Church, was he not holding his left hand under [1245D] her head? For the left [1246A] hand is set for adversity. By this left hand, then, by this adversity, by this most hard death of our Savior, we have been lifted up out of the mire of the deep and out of the utmost misery. For when with bowed head he gave up the spirit, he doubtless raised our head to himself. And his right hand embraced the Church, because, rising from the dead and made immortal, he took up again by his right hand and his strength all the things which indeed he drew to himself. And we may also understand by the left hand those things which are necessary to this life, and by the right hand that highest [sic: *beatitudiuem*]. For while we live in this world, the Lord holds as it were his left hand under our head, sustaining us in adversity and supplying what is needful. But after we leave this life, embraced by the right hand of God, clothed with immortality and strength, nothing sinister, [1246B] nothing adverse will any longer be able to touch us. The voice of Christ:

« I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes and the harts of the fields, that you stir not up, nor make to awake my beloved, till she herself will. » What is meant by the daughters of Jerusalem, if not all the souls regenerated in the font of baptism? What by the roes and the harts, if not the virtues and good works, by which we both run to heaven and overcome the venom of serpents and of demons? And what by the beloved, if not the soul that is at leisure for the contemplation of God alone? For to rouse her from so great a sleep, to part her from so great a quiet and so great a blessedness, unless she herself will it or necessity compel it, is a sin. He therefore who loves the harts and the roes, who dreads to lose feet, wings, strength, and equity, let him not be troublesome to this beloved of God. [1246C] Verses: As among the trees the apple, pleasing in fruits and in odor,
So is my beloved in the sole assembly of the sons.
Under his shadow I sat, in refreshment I rested.
Apples sweet to my throat I received from him.
He brought me into the cellar, and bade me drink wine.
He gave me charity, the mother of all the virtues.
By his left hand the head is lifted up, by his right hand the head is embraced.
Besides this, unless he loved me, who would adjure me for his sake?
The voice of the Church: « The voice of my beloved. » This, she says,
is the voice, this which I hear, the adjuration of my beloved. For unless
he had loved me, he would in no wise have spoken thus for me.


« Behold, he cometh. » But how shall he come? « Leaping [1246D] upon the mountains. » For coming from the heavens he gave his first [1247A] leap into the womb of the Virgin. This is that stone which is said to have been cut out of the mountain without hands. For without the embraces of a man Christ came forth from the Virgin.
